title: Approaches to involve the public in interpretation of findings from systematic reviews on health interventions at the population level
summary:
Background
Systematic reviews summarize the results of all studies on a specific research question. They are “studies of studies” and provide an overview of the current state of knowledge. Patients and members of the public are increasingly being involved in research—including in systematic reviews. Some systematic reviews analyze public health measures that target the general population, such as a sugar tax. Citizens should be involved in these systematic reviews. Their participation is particularly important in the discussion and interpretation of the results, in order to understand whether, in the citizens’ view, the research findings justify the political implementation of measures (such as the introduction of a sugar tax). To do this, however, citizens must first have a good understanding of the results of systematic reviews. The project aims to determine which of three communication formats—a summary in lay language, a fact box, or a simulation format—is best suited to engage citizens in interpreting the results of systematic reviews at the population level. 


Methods
The project consists of two studies: an online survey and moderated group discussions. First, during the preparatory phase, a team of researchers and citizens—who will participate as co-researchers—will be formed. Together, the team will select two population-level health interventions. Next, three communication formats will be developed to summarize the results of systematic reviews on these two topics: a summary in lay language, a fact box, and a simulation format. In an online survey, these formats will be tested on a group that reflects the German population in terms of gender, age, and education. The participants in the online survey indicate how well they understand the formats. The format that receives the highest rating will then be used in four discussion sessions with citizens to test how citizen participation works in practice when interpreting the results of systematic reviews at the population level. Two of the sessions will take place online and two in person. Among other things, the participants discuss whether the measures would be meaningful in Germany. At the end, there is an evaluation of the entire study, and researchers and co-researchers assess the process. The project will last a total of two years.
